title: Eye Massage and Pressure Points for Eye Strain From Screens — cv.cm
description: Six pressure points around the eyes, pressed on the bone and never on the eyeball, plus palming, a 3-minute routine, the 20-20-20 rule and when to see an eye doctor.
h1: Which pressure points help with eye strain?
answer: For tired eyes from screens, the usual points sit on the bony rim around the eye: `BL2` at the inner end of the eyebrow, Yuyao in the middle of the brow, `TE23` at the outer end, `GB1` beside the outer corner of the eye, `ST2` on the cheekbone and Taiyang at the temple. Press lightly on the bone, never on the eyeball, and take regular screen breaks.

sections.h: What eye strain is, and what helps most
body: Eye strain from screens shows up as tired, achy, dry or stinging eyes, blurry vision after long focus, and sometimes a headache across the brow. The American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) says it is uncomfortable but does not cause lasting damage to the eyes. It is no different from the strain you get from reading or driving for hours.

The main causes are long focus at one distance and blinking less. The AAO reports that people blink about 15 times a minute normally, but only about 5 to 7 times a minute while using screens. Because of this, the most useful steps are breaks and blinking. Gentle pressure around the eyes and warm palms can make the break more relaxing. They do not replace the breaks.

All six points sit on bone or in a small hollow of bone around the eye socket. Locations follow the WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations (2008). Yuyao and Taiyang are traditional extra points outside that list. A cun is about the width of your thumb at the knuckle. Press both sides at the same time.

body.note: Never press on the eyeball or the soft eyelid, and never push into the eye socket under the brow or above the cheekbone. All pressure goes onto bone. Take out contact lenses first, and wash your hands.

body: Use light pressure, about 2 to 4 on a 1 to 10 scale: the skin moves and you feel the bone, but nothing hurts. The skin around the eyes is thin, so press, do not rub hard or drag the skin.

sections.h: Palming: warm hands over closed eyes
body: Palming is a simple way to rest the eyes. It is relaxing and it blocks light. It does not change your eyesight.

ol: Rub your palms together for about 10 seconds until they feel warm.
Cup the palms over the eyes, with the heels of the hands on the cheekbones and the fingers on the forehead. The palms should not touch or press the eyelids.
Breathe slowly and rest for 30 to 60 seconds in the dark.
Lower the hands and open the eyes slowly.

body: Do this in a break from the screen, for example after every one or two pomodoro blocks. A timer helps you remember: for example, cv.cm's pomodoro timer can signal a break every 25 to 50 minutes.

head: Step
What to do
Time
rows: Look at something at least 6 metres (20 feet) away and blink slowly
Press upward on the inner ends of the brows
Small circles at the middle, then the outer end of the brows
Very light circles beside the eyes, then on the temples
Light circles on the cheekbone below each eye
Warm palms cupped over closed eyes
Ten full, slow blinks, closing the eyes completely

sections.h: Screen habits that matter more than any point
body: These steps come from the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

ul: Use the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look at something at least 20 feet (about 6 metres) away for at least 20 seconds.
Blink on purpose. A note on the edge of the screen can remind you.
Sit about 25 inches (about 63 cm), roughly an arm's length, from the screen, and set the screen so you look slightly down.
Match the screen brightness to the room, and raise the contrast.
Reduce glare from windows and lamps.
If your eyes feel dry, artificial tears and a humidifier can help. Keep vents from blowing air into your face.
If you wear contact lenses, give your eyes a break with glasses on long screen days.

body: Make sure your glasses or contact lens prescription is up to date. A wrong prescription is a common cause of eye strain.

sections.h: What the evidence says, including China's eye exercises
body: There are few good studies of pressure points for adult eye strain. Most of the research is on China's school eye exercises (眼保健操), a short daily routine of pressing points around the eyes that schools in China have used for decades.

A 2015 randomised trial in Chinese school children found that the standard exercises reduced a measure of eye focusing effort slightly more than sham points or simply closing the eyes. The authors judged the effect to be statistically significant but probably not clinically important. A 2016 study in Anyang, central China, followed about 200 children for two years and found no clear link between doing the exercises and the start or worsening of short-sightedness.
So treat eye-area pressure as a pleasant way to take a break, not as a way to protect or improve your eyesight. The breaks, blinking and screen setup above are what the eye-health bodies recommend.

sections.h: Safety: when to see an eye doctor
body: Do not press around the eyes if you have an eye infection, a stye, a red or swollen eyelid, a recent eye operation or injury, or broken skin. If you have glaucoma or have had eye surgery, ask your eye doctor before pressing near the eyes.

body.note: Get urgent eye care if you have sudden loss of vision or sudden blurred vision, eye pain, new flashes of light or a shower of new floaters, a shadow or curtain over part of your vision, or a red, painful eye, especially with light sensitivity. Call your local emergency number if vision loss comes with weakness, numbness or trouble speaking.

body: Book an appointment with an eye doctor or optometrist if eye strain keeps coming back after you have changed your screen habits, if your eyes are often red, blurry, watery or sensitive to light, or if you get double vision or headaches when you read.

faq.q: Is it safe to massage your eyes?
faq.a: Massage around the eyes, not on them. Press lightly on the bony rim and the eyebrows, and never press the eyeball or eyelid. Skip it if the eye is red, infected or recently operated on.
No. There is no good evidence that pressure points or eye exercises improve eyesight or prevent short-sightedness. They can make a screen break more relaxing.

faq.q: How do you get rid of eye strain fast?
faq.a: Stop looking at the screen, look far away, blink fully a few times, and rest the eyes with warm palms for a minute. If it keeps returning, check your screen setup and your glasses prescription.
Yes. Long focus can cause a dull ache across the brow and forehead. A sudden severe headache, or one with vision loss or eye pain, needs urgent medical care.

faq.q: Do warm compresses help tired eyes?
faq.a: Many people find a warm, clean, damp cloth over closed eyes soothing for a few minutes. Make sure it is warm, not hot, and do not use one on an infected eye.
